knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Permanent structures such as the tree ring and paved corner are subtracted from the bed rectangle: 18 minus 1 minus 2 gives 15 square metres of planting area before the depth is applied.
A suspect load is kept separate and recorded, and the supplier is contacted. Spreading it or burying the timber would spread contamination or hide a hazard.
Mulch piled on stems and crowns can cause rot and kill shrubs. A clear ring around each plant is the correct finish.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied mock bed plan with a trunk ring and a paved corner, the learner calculates the planting area and the volume at a supplied depth, showing the working, within the assessor's set time.
The learner inspects a supplied mock delivery with a painted timber piece and separates the suspect material from the load.
The learner spreads mock mulch around a supplied mock shrub and trunk, leaving a clear ring around each stem.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Signed calculation sheet for the mock bed.
Assessor record of the delivery check and separation.
Assessor observation record of the spreading demonstration.
stopWorkCriteria: Spreading the suspect mock load during the assessment.
Piling mock mulch against a mock stem or crown during the assessment.
